title: Residue-controlled uniform bounds for finite internal Homs
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer with $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. On the small pro-etale site of $X$ put $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$, $B_n=(A_n)_X$ for $n\geq1$ and $B=\varprojlim_nB_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $K,L\in D^b_c(X,R)$ in the derived-complete integral sense [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and write $K_n=K\otimes_B^LB_n$ and $L_n=L\otimes_B^LB_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].

Let $\alpha\leq\beta$ and $\gamma\leq\epsilon$ be integers such that $\mathcal H^i(K_1)=0$ for $i\notin[\alpha,\beta]$ and $\mathcal H^i(L_1)=0$ for $i\notin[\gamma,\epsilon]$ [def-weil-cohomological-support]. For every $n\geq1$ form only the finite-coefficient internal Hom
$$
 T_n=R\mathcal Hom_{B_n}(K_n,L_n)\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)
$$
[def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then every $T_n$ is bounded constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], has Tor amplitude over $B_n$ in the single interval
$$
 I=[\gamma-\beta-2d,\epsilon-\alpha+2d]
$$
[def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], and satisfies $\mathcal H^i(T_n)=0$ for every $i\notin I$. The same $I$ works for all $n\geq1$.

source.place: Proof, sentences 2–3 and final sentence; the uniform finite-level estimate before integral Hom reconstruction

proof.text: For every $n\geq1$, the definition of $D^b_c(X,R)$ makes $K_n$ and $L_n$ bounded constructible. The image of $\ell$ in $k$ is nonzero since $\ell\ne p$, and its inverse in $k$ maps under the structure morphism to an inverse on $X$; thus $\ell$ is invertible on $X$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] first to $K$ with $[a,b]=[\alpha,\beta]$ and then to $L$ with $[a,b]=[\gamma,\epsilon]$. Its hypotheses are exactly integral constructibility and the two given level-one cohomology bounds. It gives Tor amplitude $[\alpha,\beta]$ for every $K_n$ and $[\gamma,\epsilon]$ for every $L_n$, over their respective $B_n$. Together with bounded constructibility, these are the defining conditions for $K_n,L_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

source.place: Sentence 2: input reductions are finite-Tor, retaining the residue intervals

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $n\geq1$. Apply the pro-etale clause of [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] to the coefficient stage $A=A_n$, the separated finite-type scheme $X$, the supplied bound $\dim X\leq d$, and the objects $K_n,L_n$ from step 1. Take $(a,b,c,e)=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\epsilon)$ in its quantitative clause. It gives that $T_n=R\mathcal Hom_{B_n}(K_n,L_n)$ is bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude in $[\gamma-\beta-2d,\epsilon-\alpha+2d]=I$. This is on the given pro-etale site and over $B_n$, as required. The endpoints depend only on the four supplied residue bounds and on $d$, so the same interval works for all $n$.

source.place: Sentence 3: constructibility and the uniform finite internal-Hom interval

proof.text: Test the Tor-amplitude assertion of step 2 against the $B_n$-module sheaf $B_n$ placed in degree zero [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. The derived tensor in this test is $T_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_n\cong T_n$: with the K-flat representative $P$ used in [def-weil-derived-tensor], the termwise maps $P\otimes_{B_n}B_n\to P$, $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, and $P\to P\otimes_{B_n}B_n$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, are inverse chain maps by the tensor balancing relation and $B_n$-linearity of the differential. Thus $\mathcal H^i(T_n)=0$ for $i\notin I$. This argument applies to every $n\geq1$.

source.place: Final sentence: the uniform cohomological-support condition follows by the tensor-unit test

Shape: one commit holding the item and the report, with no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps, blueprint and source are unchanged from side-live, where the item is still unsplit, so the delivery is not superseded. The item is not on the route-pivot dropped list and has no repair note. There is no cycle: the item is not in the closure of its proof_deps. The route is exactly sentences 2–3 of the main-20261015 cor-coef-integral-internal-hom.proof.md: residue-Tor lemma, then the finite internal-Hom corollary. Both cited nodes are in the item's own unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed. Step 1: lem-coef-integral-residue-tor's hypotheses hold. ℓ is invertible on a k-scheme because char k = p ≠ ℓ. K is integral D^b_c. Its K_n is K⊗^L over the completed coefficient sheaf with (A_n)_X, the same object as the item's K_n since B is that completed sheaf. The level-one cohomology bounds are given. So every K_n and L_n has the same Tor interval at every level, and with bounded constructibility from def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed this is D^b_ctf(X,A_n) by def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude. Step 2: the pro-étale clause of cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom has the same coefficient ring A_n, the same pro-étale site and the same hypotheses (separated, finite type, dim ≤ d). With (a,b,c,e) = (α,β,γ,ε) its quantitative clause gives exactly I = [γ−β−2d, ε−α+2d], with no n in the endpoints. Step 3: testing the Tor amplitude against B_n in degree 0 gives the support condition. It is elementary, with the unit isomorphism written out on a K-flat representative. Small cases: K = L = R/ϖ over a point gives [α,β] = [−1,0], and RHom(K_n,K_n) lies in [−1,1] = I, so the bound holds and is sharp. I also checked d = 0 (the perfect-complex duality bound), n = 1, X = ∅ and zero inputs. No SGA source is cited, and there are no duplicates. No changes or fixes.
